chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Al-Hasan Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from one of our companions whose name Al-Hasan ibn Ali forgot, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: Three people behind whom one should not pray: the unknown (person), the exaggerator (in attributes) even if he says what you say, and the one who openly commits sin even if he is moderate (in other matters).

key_terms.الْغَالِي: The exaggerator, one who overstates the divine attributes or status of the Imams.
key_terms.الْمَجْهُولُ: The unknown person, whose reliability in transmitting hadith or leading prayer is not established.
key_terms.الْمُجَاهِرُ بِالْفُسُوقِ: The one who openly commits sin, displaying public immorality or major sins.
key_terms.صَلَّى خَلْفَهُمْ: To pray behind them, referring to following an Imam in congregational prayer.

ai.seo_question: Who are the three types of people behind whom one should not pray according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three categories to emphasize that congregational prayer requires not just theological correctness, but also verifiable reliability (thiqa) and public moral integrity. The inclusion of the 'exaggerator' (ghali) even when agreeing with you underscores the Shia caution against theological innovation that may distort the Imams' true status, while the 'openly sinful' individual illustrates that public scandal (mujahir) undermines one's authority as a prayer leader despite personal piety.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-193 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtayn, on the authority of Amr ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Khalaf ibn Himmad, on the authority of one of our companions called al-Hassan ibn Ali, on the authority of Abi As-Sadiq Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “You should not stand to pray behind three people: an unfamiliar person; someone who ascribes certain boastful attributes to the Divine Leaders, even if he expresses the same beliefs as you do; and one who is corrupt even if he is not boastful about the Divine Leaders.”
